Despite being ardent purist, sadly I must concur that emulation is the way to go in the current year. The original hardware is breaking down with age and is becoming ever more expensive to replace due to scarcity, and used copies of many of the best titles cost almost as much as they did new.

I didn't realize just how dire the state of affairs was until buying some SNES games that I never got to play as a kid from a game trader. Not a single one worked; the contacts on the cartridges were worn down to the circuit board. I can only imagine what the consoles are like (to be fair, the connector can be replaced).

My biggest turnoff with emulation used to be the lack of CRT emulation beyond basic headache-inducing scanlines, as old 256x224 games really don't look good at perfect pixel sharpness scaled up to fit a 1080p screen. Apparently there are some wicked good shaders that solve this problem now (see link). With that, I think you're better off not putting any more miles on your original hardware and just building a cheap HTPC for emulators.
